content:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a ~12% p99 reg in the JSON-mode toolcall benchmark after the kernel-selector change on stage. Not sure if it's a batching mismatch or KV-cache churn.
Mona: ugh. which kernel change? the SIMD fallback we rolled earlier?
Alex: yeah, the patch that prefers kernel_B for short sequences. bench-run id: br-20260317-3
Tim: can you paste the run config? is this synthetic replay or live trace?
Alex: replay harness using sampled production traces (15k sessions). config snippet: `kernel_policy=prefer_B_for_len<=64, max_batch_tokens=4096, batch_timeout_ms=8`
Caro: quick note — JSON-mode does validation + reserialize which adds some CPU per token. but 12% p99 seems high for CPU-only.
Samir: what were KV cache hit rates during the run? if cache misses spike, kernel selection could push more long-context paths.
Alex: KV hits dropped from 96% -> 88% around the regression window. correlates with increased tail.
Mona: that could be from batching heuristics — prefer_B reduces per-request token count so batching groups different seq lengths resulting in more cache eviction?
Tim: hypothesis: prefer_B changes memory layout -> more frequent chunk boundary evictions during replay (our replay timing is a bit more bursty).
bench-bot: run br-20260317-3 completed. avg latency +6.8%, p99 +11.7%, KV-hit 88.1%, cpu% 72
Caro: can we reproduce with synthetic uniform traffic? we should do apples-to-apples: same arrival distribution, same seed ordering.
Samir: I'll kick off a synthetic run that matches the replay's inter-arrival distribution (bursty Poisson) and a pure uniform run for comparison.
Alex: also include a run toggling `batch_timeout_ms=2/8/20` and `max_batch_tokens=2k/4k/8k` to see sensitivity.
Mona: include a control where kernel_selector=legacy (pre-change) so we can diff kernels only.
Tim: important: disable JSON validation for one run (if safe) to measure validator overhead and detect how many requests would fail validation -> retries.
Caro: good call. add a flag `json_validate=false` and collect validation_fail_rate. if validation fails cause retries, that inflates tail.
Samir: launching 6 runs now: replay+legacy, replay+new, synthetic+new, synthetic+legacy, replay+new+no-validate, replay+new+small-timeout. ETA ~45m.
Alex: while runs are spinning, I dug into profiler samples from the regression window: more time in memcpy and kernel dispatch syscall. might be batching coalescing issue.
Mona: do we have tracing that tags which kernel was selected per request? would help attribute latency to kernel_B.
Tim: yes — runtime emits `kernel_choice` tag. Alex, can you grep traces for `kernel_choice=kernel_B` and p99 buckets?
Alex: done. p99 of kernel_B requests is 20% higher than kernel_A for same input length. but kernel_B is supposed to be faster for <=64. suspicious.
Caro: maybe the kernel binary we shipped had suboptimal launch overhead on our GPU driver version. any infra-bot alerts?
infra-bot: GPU driver 525.92 rolled onto stage 2026-03-15 02:14 UTC on pool-stage-3. No other infra changes reported.
Samir: driver change could interact with kernel launch latency. we should do an A/B on driver version too but that's heavier.
Mona: short-term, can we fallback to legacy kernel for JSON-mode requests only? that would be a targeted mitigation.
Alex: agreed. also adding more aggressive KV cache prefetch for small sequences might reduce misses.
Tim: after synthetic runs finish, let's compare apples-to-apples: p50/p95/p99, kv-hit, cpu/gpu utilization, and validation_fail_rate. record run tags in bench dashboard.
bench-bot: synthetic run br-20260317-3a completed. p99 delta (new vs legacy): +9.8% (replay) vs +3.2% (synthetic). KV-hit drop only visible in replay.
Caro: that suggests replay timing exposes a batching pattern that hurts KV retention. maybe replay's shorter inter-request gaps create more partial batches and more KV churn.
Samir: I pulled batch composition heatmaps — new kernel increases heterogeneity in batch sequence lengths by ~18%, leading to more padding and misaligned KV lifetimes.
Alex: plan: 1) revert kernel selector for <=64 on stage for now, 2) tune batching to prefer homogenous-length groups (heuristic: group by length bucket before fill), 3) add KV cache metrics per-batch to detect churn earlier.
Mona: add also a small test that toggles json_validate to measure retries count. if validation failures are non-trivial we might need to optimize the validator or move it off hot path.
Tim: I'll file a quick perf bug with reproducer and run diffs. posting the reproducer command:
`./bench_replay --run-id br-20260317-3 --kernel_policy prefer_B_for_len<=64 --batch_timeout_ms=8 --max_batch_tokens=4096`
Alex: thanks. leaving a note to not rollout any kernel selector changes until perf + kv metrics look stable. :eyes:
Mona: if anyone has quick wins, fallback by route (json-mode) is the least blast radius.
Samir: I'll collect the full artifact bundle (profiles, batch heatmaps, kv traces) and upload to the bench bucket at s3://redwood-bench/br-20260317-3/artifacts.tar.gz
Caro: great. after we stabilize on stage, we should run the same set on a dedicated pool to ensure dedicated/different memory pressure doesn't hide it.
Alex: perfect. thanks team.
Tim: +1, and let's capture exact kernel binaries (sha) in the run metadata next time to avoid ambiguity.
bench-bot: artifact upload complete: s3://redwood-bench/br-20260317-3/artifacts.tar.gz
Alex: closing for now — will update when rollback is in and we have contrast runs. :thumbsup:
